$doc: Vyomi capability registry — GCP Firestore. See aws/s3.json for the contract. Feature ids share one namespace with the AWS registry, so they are prefixed gcp.firestore.*

gcp.firestore.databases.title: Databases (list, create, get, update, delete)
limitations: Database create/update/delete complete synchronously in Vyomi; the real API returns a long-running operation to poll.

gcp.firestore.documents.title: Collections and documents (create, get, list, merge, delete) and the Firestore Studio data viewer

gcp.firestore.query-builder.title: Query builder (structured queries: field filters, composite AND/OR, orderBy, limit)

gcp.firestore.indexes.title: Composite indexes (create, list, delete)
limitations: Indexes report state READY immediately; Vyomi does not model the real console's transient BUILDING phase, and it does not reject queries that would need a missing index.

gcp.firestore.single-field-exemptions.title: Single-field index exemptions
limitations: Exempting a field now really disables its automatic index: a query that needs the removed index (an inequality, orderBy or array-contains on that field) fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION unless a composite index covers it, matching the real service.

The composite-index coverage check only matches an exact field-path + order/arrayConfig pair; it does not model the full multi-field prefix matching real Firestore uses to pick a usable composite index.

gcp.firestore.vector-indexes.title: Vector indexes (for vector-similarity search)
limitations: Vyomi has no vector field type or similarity search engine, so vector indexes cannot be created or used.

gcp.firestore.ttl.title: Time-to-live (TTL) policies
limitations: Expiry is checked lazily — on the next access to the owning database — rather than by a continuously running background process; real Firestore's own TTL sweep is likewise best-effort and not immediate, so the functional difference is only in timing, not outcome.

gcp.firestore.security-rules.title: Security rules editor
limitations: Vyomi stores and returns the rules source exactly as written through its own getSecurityRules/updateSecurityRules endpoints (real Firestore security rules are managed by the separate Firebase Rules API), but it never evaluates the rules against a request — every document read/write Vyomi allows is unconditional.

Real Firestore only evaluates rules against end-user client-SDK requests — the Admin SDK, gcloud and the console's own Data viewer always bypass them. Vyomi's native wire has no notion of a client-vs-admin caller (the console itself is one of the callers), so evaluating rules against it would lock the console out of its own data viewer rather than model the real behavior.

gcp.firestore.import-export.title: Import / Export (exportDocuments / importDocuments)
limitations: Export really writes a Cloud Storage object (via Vyomi's own GCS simulator) and import really reads it back, but the file is a Vyomi-internal JSON snapshot, not the real protobuf/LevelDB export layout — the object isn't portable to a real `gcloud firestore import`.

gcp.firestore.backups.title: Backup schedules and backups
limitations: Creating a backup schedule is real and immediately takes one backup (there is no background scheduler in Vyomi to fire later ticks on the daily/weekly recurrence).
`databases:restore` now really repopulates a brand-new database's documents, indexes and fields from the backup's snapshot, synchronously (the real API returns a long-running operation).

gcp.firestore.point-in-time-recovery.title: Point-in-time recovery (PITR)
limitations: While enabled, Vyomi keeps a per-document version history and `documents.get` / `documents.list` / `:runQuery` / `:batchGet` honor a `readTime` in the past, really returning the document as it was at that time.
There is no one-click whole-database PITR restore into a new database (unlike backup restore) — recovering a prior state means reading documents at that `readTime` yourself.

gcp.firestore.insights.title: Insights (query and index usage recommendations)
limitations: Vyomi collects no query-performance telemetry, so it has nothing to generate index or query insights from.

gcp.firestore.usage.title: Usage dashboard (reads/writes/deletes/storage charts)
limitations: Vyomi meters real running totals (reads, writes, deletes, current document count and an estimated storage size) via a dedicated `:usage` endpoint, but keeps no history, so it cannot render the real console's over-time charts built from Cloud Monitoring metrics.

gcp.firestore.key-visualizer.title: Key Visualizer
limitations: Key Visualizer renders a heatmap of real production key-access load; Vyomi records no per-key traffic histograms to visualize.
